title: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)

sections.label: Economy 2022 and 2023 outlook
sections.summary: The Member moves to reduce Head V of the Estimates by $100 and asks how the economy fared in 2022 and the outlook for 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head V of the Estimates be reduced by $100." Sir, as in every MTI COS debate, we start by taking stock of the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: So, let me kick off by asking the Minister on how has the economy fared in 2022 and what he sees as the outlook for 2023.

sections.label: Singapore navigating uncertain environment
sections.summary: The Member asks the Minister how Singapore would navigate and respond to an increasingly complex and uncertain operating environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, can I ask the Minister how would Singapore navigate and respond to this increasingly complex and uncertain operating environment?

sections.label: Vaccine plants in Singapore
sections.summary: Before the pandemic Singapore had no vaccine-producing facility, but five pharmaceutical companies will set up plants here within two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Before the pandemic, we do not have a single facility that produce vaccine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: But in the next two years, five pharmaceutical companies will be setting up plants here, which can churn out a billion doses of vaccines annually.

sections.label: National Productivity Fund top-up
sections.summary: The National Productivity Fund is topped up by $4 billion and its scope expanded to include investment promotion as a supportable activity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The $4 billion top up of the National Productivity Fund, which has had its scope expanded to include investment promotion as a supportable activity, is one of the new tool kits.

sections.label: Export and offshore trade targets
sections.summary: The aim is to grow export value from $805 billion to at least $1 trillion and double offshore trade value from US$1 trillion to US$2 trillion from 2020 to 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Among other things, we aim to grow our export value from $805 billion to at least $1 trillion from 2020 to 2030 and double our offshore trade value from US$1 trillion to US$2 trillion over the same period.

sections.label: Measuring National Productivity Fund success
sections.summary: The Member notes the $4 billion top-up and expanded scope, compares the sum to MND and MSF spending, and asks how success will be measured.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Wong mentioned that the National Productivity Fund will be topped up with an additional $4 billion and the scope of the fund will be expanded to include investment promotion as a supporting activity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Given that $4 billion is half of what we spend on the Ministry of National Development (MND) and about the same amount that we spend on the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), what will be the measure of success for the National Productivity Fund?

sections.label: Silver economy market projection
sections.summary: An Enterprise Singapore blog article stated the Asia Pacific silver economy market was projected to be worth US$4.6 trillion by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In a recent blog article published by Enterprise Singapore entitled "Silver economy: Is the business of ageing a sunrise industry?", the author pointed out that in the Asia Pacific region, the silver economy market was projected to be worth US$4.6 trillion by 2025, just two years from now.

sections.label: Biomedical researchers per capita
sections.summary: Figures from 2018 showed Singapore employs five times more biomedical researchers per capita than the US.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, figures from 2018 showed that we employ five times more biomedical researchers per capita than the US.

sections.label: Gut microbiome research support
sections.summary: The passage says startup research into precision gut microbiomes deserves full support, citing efforts for a transplant bank and Asian database.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Thus, the research and innovative work done by startups and early stage companies into precision gut microbiomes here in Singapore deserves our full support.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I believe that there are currently efforts to maintain Southeast Asia's first and only gut microbiome transplant bank, along with building the world's largest multi-ethnic Asian gut microbiome database.

sections.label: Clarification on talent schemes
sections.summary: The speaker seeks clarification on the success rate of schemes training Singaporeans to lead biomedical and biotech companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While I note Minister of State Low Yen Ling's reply to me in a Parliamentary Question (PQ) outlining the steps taken to address concerns over potential manpower and talent shortages, particularly at the senior, C-suite levels, I would like further clarification about the success rate of our schemes after more than two decades in training Singaporeans to equip enough of us with the right skillsets to be able to found, lead and expand our companies to make Singapore a prominent player within the biomedical and biotech fields.

sections.label: Sustainability in Enterprise Innovation scheme
sections.summary: The passage suggests the Enterprise Innovation scheme could integrate sustainability into tax deduction criteria and co-investment fund grants.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, the Enterprise Innovation scheme could have sustainability integrated as part of the criteria for tax deductions as well as for grants under the co-investment fund.

sections.label: EXIM Bank for green transition
sections.summary: The passage says an EXIM Bank could help businesses in the green transition, noting calls for such a bank and potential competitive advantage.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The role of such a bank can be particularly helpful as we move along the great green transition, where we can seek help for our businesses in a changing world where climate concerns take front and centre.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We further noted that while former MTI Minister Lim Hng Kiang expressed reservations about financial and implementation risks that would be involved in setting up an EXIM Bank, apart from the Workers' Party's proposals, MTI's own Economic Strategies Committee has also called for such a bank.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Additionally, structuring an EXIM bank well could in fact give us a key competitive advantage.

sections.label: EXIM banks green financing
sections.summary: Many EXIM banks from China to Thailand and Hungary have rolled out green financing facilities, having played a role in preventing collapse during economic crises.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Many EXIM banks from China to Thailand and Hungary have also rolled out green financing facilities, also because EXIM banks have proven to have played a role in preventing complete collapse during times of economic crisis.

sections.label: Singapore addressing data challenges
sections.summary: These can be used to address data challenges causing gaps in regional or global green and sustainability financial markets, letting Singapore punch above its weight.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It can then use these to address data challenges that can cause gaps in regional or even global green and sustainability financial markets.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This would thus be a way in which Singapore can use to punch above our weight and bringing the world along in the transition to green financing.

sections.label: Measures for local SMEs
sections.summary: The passage asks what measures the Government took to help local SMEs tide through the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: During such challenging circumstances, what measures did the Government take to help local SMEs tide through the COVID-19 pandemic?

sections.label: US Federal Funds Rate pricing
sections.summary: Financial markets are pricing the US Federal Funds Rate to reach 5.25%, and businesses' interest burden is expected to at least double compared to last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Financial markets are currently pricing the US Federal Funds Rate to reach 5.25%, reinforcing the view that interest rates will remain higher for longer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The interest burden for businesses are expected to at least be double compared to last year.

sections.label: SMEs and interest rate subsidies
sections.summary: SMEs are vulnerable to interest rate hikes and want to know if MTI will consider continued interest rate subsidies under the Enterprise Financing Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Generally, SMEs are vulnerable to interest rate hikes and are keen to know if MTI will consider continued interest rate subsidies under the Enterprise Financing Scheme before they decide on whether to take more risk to pursue growth opportunities?

sections.label: Shortening payment terms for SMEs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MTI will consider allowing SMEs to negotiate a temporary shortening of payment terms or payment advancement over a limited period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will MTI consider allowing SMEs to negotiate a temporary shortening of payment terms or payment advancement over a limited period?

sections.label: National Productivity Fund top-up
sections.summary: The $4 billion top-up to the National Productivity Fund will support productivity enhancements and worker reskilling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The $4 billion top-up to the National Productivity Fund (NPF) will help to support the much-needed productivity enhancements and the reskilling of workers.

sections.label: Enterprise Innovation Scheme for SMEs
sections.summary: The new Enterprise Innovation Scheme announced by the Deputy Prime Minister will reduce the financial barrier for SMEs to embark on innovation projects like SOVEG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The new Enterprise Innovation Scheme announced by Deputy Prime Minister will help reduce the financial barrier for SMEs to embark on innovation projects like SOVEG.

sections.label: Extending MRA grant to manpower costs
sections.summary: It asks whether MTI will consider SBF's recommendation to extend the Market Readiness Assistance grant to cover manpower costs for overseas market promotion, business development or market set-up activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will MTI consider SBF’s recommendation to extend the Market Readiness Assistance (MRA) grant to cover manpower costs for related overseas market promotion, business development, or market set-up activities?

sections.label: Manufacturing share of Singapore GDP
sections.summary: As of 2022, manufacturing accounts for approximately 20% of Singapore's GDP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: As of 2022, manufacturing accounts for approximately 20% of Singapore's GDP.

sections.label: Jobs Growth Initiative local hires
sections.summary: The Jobs Growth Initiative scheme was successful in encouraging local hires amidst the COVID-19 crisis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Jobs Growth Initiative (JGI) scheme was successful in encouraging local hires amidst the COVID-19 crisis.

sections.label: Skilled talent and Job-Skills Integrators
sections.summary: The talent base needs to be skilled to match growing sectors, and questions were asked on the capability, support and funding of new Job-Skills Integrators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Our talent base needs to be skilled to match the growing sectors that require talent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I had asked a list of questions on the capability of the new Job-Skills Integrators, how will they be supported and funded to work with businesses and workers.

sections.label: Higher salaries and business costs
sections.summary: Many will have to offer higher salaries or better benefits to attract and retain employees, driving up business costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: Many will have to offer higher salaries or better benefits to attract and retain employees and driving up business costs.

sections.label: Manufacturing GDP and employment shares
sections.summary: Manufacturing's share of GDP rose from about 15% in 1965 to nearly 30% by the early 1980s, declining since the late 1980s to around 20% today, while its employment share has declined since around 1990 to around 12%.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the manufacturing share of total GDP increased from about 15% in 1965 to nearly 30% by the early 1980s, but it has been declining since the late 1980s to hover around 20% today.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The vision of Manufacturing 2030 is to be a global business innovation and talent hub for Advanced Manufacturing.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, while the manufacturing sector share of total GDP has stayed around 20%, its share of total resident employment has been on a steady decline since around 1990 and now hovers around 12%.

sections.label: Manufacturing GDP and services jobs
sections.summary: Manufacturing contributes 20% to 25% of annual GDP, while the diversified services sector represented 74.1% of jobs at end-2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Manufacturing contributes 20% to 25% of annual Gross Domestic Product (GDP), while our diversified services sector represented 74.1% of jobs at end-2022.

sections.label: Advanced Manufacturing exports and carbon transition
sections.summary: The Advanced Manufacturing sector is known for exporting petrochemicals, pharmaceuticals and precision engineering products, but carbon transition changes will disrupt this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Our Advanced Manufacturing sector is well-known for exporting petrochemicals, pharmaceuticals and precision engineering products but changes to carbon transition will disrupt this.

sections.label: Singapore economy and 2030 visions
sections.summary: Singapore's economy grew 3.6% in 2022, and Minister Gan revealed the Singapore Economy 2030 vision and Enterprise 2030 strategy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Singapore's economy grew by 3.6% in 2022, amid a challenging economic environment and external backdrop.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Last year in the Ministry of Trade (MTI)'s Committee of Supply (COS), Minister Gan revealed Singapore Economy 2030 vision to strengthen our local businesses for sustainable growth in the services, manufacturing and trade sectors, as well as the Enterprise 2030 strategy to foster a vibrant ecosystem of Singapore enterprises that are future-ready and globally competitive.

sections.label: Refreshed Industry Transformation Maps
sections.summary: Last year, the Industry Transformation Maps for five sectors from the Advanced Manufacturing and Trade cluster were refreshed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Last year, the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) for five sectors from the Advanced Manufacturing and Trade cluster were refreshed.

sections.label: Enterprise Development Grant administration
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore administers the Enterprise Development Grant to assist companies with transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore administers the Enterprise Development Grant (EDG) to, amongst other things, assist companies with transformation.

sections.label: SME digitalisation and green ambition
sections.summary: Budget 2022 provided $200 million for SME digitalisation, and Singapore committed to net-zero emissions by 2050 and higher carbon tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: Budget 2022 provided a big push for our SMEs in their digitalisation journey, with $200 million to enhance schemes for them to build digital capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: While this is gaining momentum, in tandem also with the commendable efforts in digitalising our heartland merchants and residents by the SG Digital Office, little has been said specifically on SME digitalisation in Budget 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: Given this, what is MTI's assessment of the digitalisation progress of our SMEs so far?

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: What initiatives and measures is the Minister considering to further accelerate the digitalisation of SMEs in this Budget?

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, over the past year, Singapore has clearly stepped up in its green ambition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: We have committed to net-zero emissions by 2050 and passed the Carbon Price (Amendment) Bill in this House.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: We will raise carbon tax from $5 per tonne of emissions to $50 to $80 by 2030 to provide an economy-wide price signal to reduce emissions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The public sector has also stepped up and made the commitment to reach net-zero carbon emissions five years earlier, by 2045.

sections.label: EFS-Green loan terms expectations
sections.summary: The Government shares up to 70% of risk with partner financial institutions under EFS-Green.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: With the Government sharing up to 70% of the risk with partner financial institutions, I would like to ask the Minister what expectations have been laid down with participating financial institutions to provide preferential loan terms and interest rates under EFS-Green?

sections.label: Decarbonising power sector priority
sections.summary: Singapore has committed to energy efficiency and decarbonisation, with the power sector a priority because it produces 40% of emissions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Despite our challenges, Singapore has committed to drive energy efficiency and to decarbonise.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But because 40% of our overall emissions comes from the power sector, decarbonising the power sector therefore has to be an even more urgent priority.

sections.label: Carbon tax transition framework
sections.summary: Budget 2022 announced a revised carbon tax framework from 2024 and a transition framework for emissions-intensive trade-exposed companies.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At Budget 2022, the Singapore Government announced a revised carbon tax framework effective from 2024.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It also announced a transition framework to give existing emissions-intensive trade-exposed companies (EITE) more time to adjust to our new carbon tax policy, and to help maintain their business competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Government elaborate on the efficiency standards and decarbonisation targets that EITE companies would have to meet to receive transitory allowances for part of their emissions?

sections.label: Pull factors for SME green transition
sections.summary: MTI was asked to explain pull factors to encourage SMEs in their green transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: As transformation requires not just a push factor like carbon tax, can MTI further explain the pull factors that will be put in place to encourage and help SMEs in their green transition so that they can stay relevant and capture opportunities in the green economy?

sections.label: Expanding schemes for SMEs
sections.summary: A speaker asks whether MTI can consider expanding current schemes and grants to spur SMEs in more sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh
sentences.text: On this note, can MTI consider expanding the scope of current schemes and grants to spur our SMEs in more sectors?

sections.label: Unit business cost rise
sections.summary: In 2022 and 2023, unit business cost in manufacturing and service sectors rose by 9.6% and 8.8% respectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: In 2022, and now in 2023, the unit business cost in manufacturing and service sectors rose by 9.6% and 8.8% respectively.

sections.label: SME sustainability reporting support
sections.summary: A speaker asks whether the Government has plans to support SMEs in their sustainability reporting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Does the Government have plans to support SMEs in their sustainability reporting?

sections.label: UPAGE represents 6,000 workers
sections.summary: As General-Secretary of UPAGE, the speaker says the union represents about 6,000 workers in the industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As a General-Secretary of Union of Power and Gas Employees, in short UPAGE, we represent about 6,000 workers in this industry, ranging from technicians, technical officers, engineers, admin assistants, managers, and even chief executive officers (CEOs).

sections.label: Appeal to reward workers
sections.summary: The speaker appeals to the Minister to consider rewarding workers, as MOH did for healthcare workers in November 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our workers also work round the clock but observed that we are hardly mentioned nor fairly rewarded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I am humbly appealing to the Minister to consider rewarding our workers for their efforts just as the Ministry of Health did for their healthcare workers earlier in November 2021.

sections.label: Workers upskilling and training hours
sections.summary: The speaker shares that 3,500 workers acquired new skills, over 800,000 training hours were achieved, and 200 completed upskilling programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our leaders led by example and stepped forward earlier to attend the designated courses and progressively brought everyone on board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am humble to share that we have succeeded in rallying 3,500 workers in acquiring new skills and achieved over 800,000 training hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Amongst them, 200 workers have completed upskilling programmes and are applying their newly acquired skills in their new jobs.

sections.label: TAC certification and ITMs
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry would consider independent standards certification for TACs, perhaps based on SCCCI's Growth and Competency Framework launched last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: Strong TACs can act as force multipliers for their respective Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs), helping to communicate their objectives to businesses in their sector and to understand and encourage participation in the various schemes under the ITMs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider introducing independent standards certification for TACs, perhaps based on the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCCI)'s Growth and Competency Framework that was launched last year?

sections.label: Merging SBF and SNEF
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry would consider merging SBF and SNEF into a unitary national-level body representing businesses at tripartite and other forums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: Even if a distinction could be made that SNEF represents labour concerns and SBF represents commercial interests, I would submit this is an entirely artificial distinction, simply because labour and manpower considerations are one of the most important commercial consideration of any business, and often, it is also the largest item of expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: Hence, is there a need for two apex TACs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to ask if the Ministry would consider merging SBF and SNEF in order to have a unitary national-level body representing businesses at tripartite and other forums.

sections.label: TAC help for hawkers and SMEs
sections.summary: States FMAS worked with CDCs on redemption procedures, over 17,000 hawkers and merchants now participate, and over 25,000 SMEs received assistance from TAC-run SME Centres in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: For example, the Federation of Merchants' Association Singapore (FMAS) worked alongside the CDCs in optimising redemption procedures and onboarding hawkers and merchants onto the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: There are now over 17,000 participating hawkers and merchants, and this would not have been possible without the help of TACs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: On the TAC's efforts in the SME front, over 25,000 SMEs received assistance from SME Centres run by TACs through business counselling, capability development workshops, and upgrading initiatives in 2022.

sections.label: TAC overseas programmes and challenges
sections.summary: States such programmes can bring skillset transfers and networking opportunities, but TACs face talent shortages and funding challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: By establishing such programmes between local and overseas companies or even between local and overseas TACs, benefits, such as skillset transfers and networking opportunities can come about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: However, the TACs face two challenges: talent shortages and funding.

sections.label: Ministry support via GlobalConnect@SBF
sections.summary: States the Ministry has done so with SBF via the GlobalConnect@SBF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Indeed, the Ministry has done so with SBF via the GlobalConnect@SBF.

sections.label: CASE prepayment loss complaints
sections.summary: States consumers suffered more than $6 million in prepayment losses since 2018, with over $645,000 reported in 2022 due to sudden business closures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to complaints received by CASE, consumers have suffered more than $6 million in prepayment losses since 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In 2022 alone, consumers reported more than $645,000 in losses due to sudden business closures.

sections.label: Accredited contractors deposit bond
sections.summary: Accredited contractors protect consumers' deposits against sudden business closure through a deposit performance bond, with 138 accredited contractors out of an estimated 6,700 renovation contractors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Accredited contractors protect consumers' deposits against sudden business closure through a deposit performance bond.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: There are currently 138 accredited contractors, but this is only a fraction of the estimated 6,700 renovation contractors operating in Singapore.

sections.label: E-commerce scam losses
sections.summary: According to the Police, more than $21 million were lost by consumers in e-commerce scams last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to the Police, more than $21 million were lost by consumers in e-commerce scams last year.

sections.label: Singapore investment and employment
sections.summary: Singapore secured $22.5 billion in Fixed Asset Investments and $6.2 billion in Total Business Expenditure, expecting over 17,000 jobs, while resident unemployment fell to 2.9% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Singapore's position as a global business hub remained strong, as companies anchored their corporate and manufacturing activities here to strengthen the resilience of their supply chains and operations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We secured record commitments of $22.5 billion in Fixed Asset Investments, in areas, such as semiconductors, aerospace and agri-food, as well as generated $6.2 billion in Total Business Expenditure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: When the committed investments are fully implemented, we expect them to create over 17,000 jobs, and more than $20 billion in value-added per year for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Our employment situation also improved, with the annual average resident unemployment rate falling to a four-year low of 2.9% in 2022.

sections.label: 2023 economic growth outlook
sections.summary: The Singapore economy is expected to grow by 0.5% to 2.5% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa also asked about the outlook for 2023 and the challenges that businesses need to prepare for.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We expect the Singapore economy to grow by 0.5% to 2.5% in 2023.

sections.label: Modern Services growth targets
sections.summary: Within this decade, the aim is to grow Value-Added from the Modern Services cluster by at least 50% and create more than 100,000 additional jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Within this decade, we aim to grow the Value-Added (VA), from the Modern Services cluster by at least 50% and create more than 100,000 additional jobs.

sections.label: Professional Services ITM 2025 launch
sections.summary: The Professional Services Industry Transformation Map 2025 was launched to strengthen Singapore's role as a leading business hub.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Today, I am pleased to announce the launch of the Professional Services Industry Transformation Map 2025, or ITM 2025, which will play an important role in strengthening Singapore's role as a leading business hub.

sections.label: Jobs and Financial Services Growth
sections.summary: From 2016 to 2021, about 134,000 resident jobs were created and Financial Services real VA grew 6.8% per annum, exceeding the 4.3% target.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: On jobs, despite the impact of COVID-19, there was a net creation of about 134,000 resident jobs from 2016 to 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The Financial Services sector achieved real VA growth of 6.8% per annum from 2016 to 2021, exceeding the real VA growth target of 4.3% set for the period from 2016 and 2020.

sections.label: Pillar 2 and Domestic Top-up Tax
sections.summary: DPM Wong announced implementing Pillar 2 from 2025 and a Domestic Top-up Tax to raise MNE groups' effective tax rate in Singapore to 15%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Wong has announced our intention to implement Pillar 2 from 2025 and introduce a Domestic Top-up Tax at the same time, to top-up the effective tax rate of MNE groups in Singapore to 15%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Giving companies notice now will allow affected MNEs time to assess the impact on their operations, and for our economic agencies to work with them to address their concerns and support their continued growth in Singapore.

sections.label: National Productivity Fund Top-up and Scope
sections.summary: The Government has topped up the National Productivity Fund and will expand its scope to include investment promotion as a supportable activity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: In this regard, the Government has topped up the National Productivity Fund, or NPF in short, and will expand its scope to include investment promotion as a supportable activity.

sections.label: iSPRINT Programme for SMEs
sections.summary: The iSPRINT programme helped about 10,000 SMEs leverage infocomm technology solutions to improve business operations and increase productivity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)

sections.label: Green Skills Committee setup
sections.summary: MTI and SkillsFuture Singapore will set up a Green Skills Committee to develop green skills, starting with sustainability reporting and energy sector areas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Therefore, MTI, in partnership with SkillsFuture Singapore will set up a Green Skills Committee to bring together industry players and training providers to develop green skills in the local workforce that are relevant to industry needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For a start, we will focus on immediate needs such as training workers to conduct sustainability reporting and equipping them with the skills to operate in new growth areas in the energy sector such as renewable energy and energy storage systems.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will continue to work closely with the industry to identify new demand areas for green skills as this platform grows.

sections.label: Singapore Economy 2030 vision path

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: In the face of rising costs, biting resource constraints and a more challenging international environment, this is the only viable path to long-term growth and success.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)

sections.label: Low-carbon electricity imports by 2035

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)

sections.label: Energy efficiency schemes and conservation
sections.summary: Schemes like the Energy Efficiency Fund and Energy Efficiency Grant help businesses become more energy efficient, and businesses and individuals must use energy-efficient equipment and conserve energy.

sentences.text: There are multiple schemes such as the Energy Efficiency Fund and Energy Efficiency Grant which help our businesses to become more energy efficient.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Business and individuals will have to play their part to use more energy-efficient equipment and conserve energy in their daily lives.

sections.label: Transforming constraints and future planning
sections.summary: Singapore's prosperity comes from transforming constraints into opportunities, and it must address immediate challenges while keeping an eye on the future to grow sustainably.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We need to address the immediate challenges of the day, but also constantly keep an eye on the future, to ensure that Singapore continues to stay relevant in this fast-changing world.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: (In English) We must constantly keep an eye on the future and think and reinvent for the long term about how we can grow sustainably.

sections.label: Sustainability pilots and Lazarus Island

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: For example, Pontiac Land Group partnered a local startup under our Singapore Tourism Accelerator to pilot a user-interface platform that integrates data on energy, water, waste and carbon emissions across Pontiac Land's four properties in Singapore and helps them to monitor their sustainability efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: And with that, I am proud to announce that Singapore has recently been certified as a sustainable destination based on the Global Sustainable Tourism Council's Destination Criteria.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: I am also happy to share that Sentosa Development Corporation will be making our Lazarus Island a light touch destination over the next three years, where visitors can experience its rustic charm while minimising their impact to biodiversity and the environment.

sentences.text: We will start this April, by launching Tiny Away Escape @ Lazarus Island by Big Tiny, comprising five eco-tourism accommodation units on the island.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
